summary: US-021: A buyer reserves the exact seats they named
description:
**As** a buyer who has chosen seats, **I want** to reserve exactly those seats, **so that** nobody else can take them while I pay.

**Priority:** P2  **Depends on:** TKT-172 (a buyer can only name seats they were shown)

**The gap.** Inventory can already claim a named seat set atomically (`POST /holds/seats`, TKT-80) and catalog can already pin those identities against a map version (ADR-029/031). But **the buyer path cannot reach it**: commerce's `ReservationCreate` carries `{organizer_id, ticket_type_id, quantity}` and nothing else, so `POST /api/commerce/reservations` — the only reservation door the storefront has — can express "three tickets" but never "A/12/7". Seated inventory is therefore reachable only by a service-to-service caller, which no buyer is.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `ReservationCreate` accepts a seat set as an alternative to `quantity`; naming both, or neither, is a 400. The GA path is untouched and its existing tests stay green.
- [ ] A seated reservation routes to inventory's seat-claim (`POST /holds/seats`), not the quantity hold, and the resulting `Reservation` echoes the seats that were actually claimed — the buyer must be able to see what they hold, and the echoed set is the claim's, never the request's.
- [ ] Price stays catalog-resolved: commerce consumes the resolved unit price for the ticket type and multiplies by the seat count (ADR-036 — commerce never recomputes a price). Amounts are integer minor units + ISO currency.
- [ ] A seat lost to a competing claimant between display and reserve returns a distinguishable conflict naming the contended seats — enough for the UI to re-render, not a bare 409.
- [ ] Idempotency behaves as it does for GA: replaying the same `Idempotency-Key` with the same seat set returns the same reservation, and inventory's canonical seat ordering means `[A,B]` and `[B,A]` replay as one claim, not two.
- [ ] Checkout over a seated reservation completes end to end (`POST /orders`), issuing tickets for the seat count, with the checkout journal and lifecycle invariants unchanged (ADR-011 / ADR-021).
- [ ] Spec declared, generated code committed before the gate, smoke coverage for the seated reservation (ADR-009 / ADR-028 / ADR-030).

Quality gates: `make check` green; `access verify-lifecycle` green; contract tests. **This ticket touches the money path** — it prices a reservation. It introduces no new pricing rule and no new PSP interaction; it multiplies the catalog-resolved unit price by a seat count.

objective.note: Without it the seat picker has nothing to submit to: seated inventory is unreachable from the only reservation endpoint a buyer can call.

scope.note: IN: the seated reservation request/response, its routing to the seat claim, its pricing, its conflict shape, its idempotency, and seated checkout. OUT: the UI (TKT-174), orphan rules (TKT-175), best-available (TKT-81), seat-aware refunds/exchanges (TKT-164).

uncertainties.note: Whether the seated variant is a new field on `ReservationCreate` (a `oneOf`-style either/or) or a separate `/reservations/seats` operation is a Planning-time call. A field on the existing schema keeps one checkout path downstream and is the presumed default; a separate path is the more reversible option if the either/or proves hard to express in the generated types. The AC constrains behaviour, not the shape.

dependencies.note: blocked-by TKT-172. Inventory's `POST /holds/seats`, the pin coordination and the checkout/journal path are all merged.

approach.note: Commerce already proxies a claim to inventory for GA. The seated variant is the same call shape against a different inventory operation; `SeatHoldCreate` already demands `{organizer_id, slot_id, seat_identities, ticket_type_id, unit_amount, currency}`, so the mapping is mechanical once the price is resolved.

first_slice.note: One buyer reserves two named seats and pays: the order completes, the seats are confirmed, a second buyer naming one of them is refused.

success.note: Demoable through the gateway with curl end to end — reserve named seats, check out, see the tickets.

context_memo.note: Baked at decomposition (2026-08-01). Re-resolve at claim; TKT-172 will have landed and may itself have amended this area.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code — floats are banned on money paths.

Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite; run `make deps` first on a clean clone). CI runs the same gate — keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate — `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

reference.summary: Epic lineage and capability map (US-017/US-018 are the seat-claim core; this epic is the buyer-facing picker)

governingAdrs.why: Catalog is the SINGLE authority for the rule-resolved unit price; commerce consumes it and never recomputes. A seated reservation must resolve the price the same way the GA one does and multiply by the seat count — deriving a price from the seat set is the violation to avoid.
Owns the claim transaction, lock order, idempotency and TTL. The seat path extends this lifecycle rather than forking it; commerce must not invent a second claim protocol for seats.

The pin/claim coordination is inventory's, done post-commit by the inventory API caller. Commerce must not pin, unpin, or reason about pins — routing to `/holds/seats` inherits all of it. Also names the lazy expired-pin sweep, which is why a seat hold can return `ExpiredPins`.

The checkout journal protocol is unchanged by seating; a seated order must land the same immutable entries. If the seat set has to appear anywhere in the journal, it is pseudonymous seat identities, not buyer data (ADR-003).
Checkout recovery state machine — a seated checkout that times out mid-payment must reach the same terminal states as a GA one, with no seat-specific escape hatch.
Contract-first: the commerce spec changes and `openapi_gen.go` is committed before the gate.
The response validator fails closed — a `Reservation` that gains a `seats` field the spec does not declare is a 5xx at runtime, not a silent extra key.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-173

**Selection reason.** Its only blocker, TKT-172, closed minutes ago; it is now the sole claimable child of TKT-35 and it blocks the remaining two (174 → 175). Nothing else is in flight.

**Blocker check.** `blocked-by TKT-172` — Done, merged as `8b009bf4`. Zero open blockers.

**Branch.** `TKT-173-seated-reservation`, cut from `origin/main` at `8b009bf4`.

**⚠️ Gate waiver.** This ticket runs **gateless** under the same owner waiver recorded on TKT-172: all four human gates waived for epic TKT-35 as a process experiment. Gate 1 given by instruction; Gate 2 resolved by the agent from the cross-model critique (most-reversible option absent a recommendation); Gate 3 self-merged after the adversarial review converges, review-guide posted first as the audit record; Gate 4 self-validated against test evidence on merged code. `config.models` routing, cross-model review, TDD red-first, `make check` before every push and after the merge, and every marker comment all stand unchanged.

**Model routing** (unchanged, from `.claude/sdlc.config.json`): plan `gpt-5.6-sol` · planReview `main-agent` · implement `main-agent` · aiReview `gpt-5.6-sol`. Both cross-model pairs differ. ✅

---

### Stop-condition pre-check — this ticket trips two of them on purpose

The standing waiver says to stop if the work would touch **money paths** or **data migrations** *in a way the ticket and plan did not anticipate*. This ticket touches both, and both are anticipated. Recording that judgement here rather than discovering it mid-implementation:

1. **Money path.** The reservation is what prices a purchase. This ticket does **not** introduce a pricing rule, a new PSP interaction, or a new amount computation — it multiplies the catalog-resolved unit price by a seat count instead of by a quantity. ADR-036 is unchanged: catalog stays the single price authority and commerce keeps consuming `resolved_price` without recomputing. The ticket's own description says so, and its AC pins it. **Proceeding.**
2. **Data migration.** Very likely required, and the reason is structural rather than incidental. `reservations` (commerce migration `0001_checkout.sql`) stores `quantity` and no seat set. The replay path (`server.go` `reserve`) deliberately answers a retried reservation **from the persisted row**, replaying inventory with the *pinned* terms — because inventory fingerprints its idempotency on the exact request, and for a seat hold that fingerprint covers the **canonical seat set** (`seatFingerprint`). So a seated reservation that does not persist its seats cannot be replayed at all: the retry would either send a different request or send nothing. A column to hold them is inherent to the feature, not scope creep. **Proceeding** — but the plan must name the migration explicitly, and if it concludes anything *beyond* an additive column on `reservations` is needed, that is unanticipated and the run stops.

Anything else the plan surfaces that touches auth or CI/deploy config stops the run.

### What the drafter is being pointed at

The gap is narrow and specific: inventory has had `POST /holds/seats` since TKT-80 and catalog has pinned seat identities since TKT-104, but `ReservationCreate` carries `{organizer_id, ticket_type_id, quantity}` and nothing else — so the only reservation door a buyer has cannot express "A/12/7". Seated inventory is reachable today only by a service-to-service caller, which no buyer is.

TKT-172 closed the *read* half of that (a buyer can now see which seats are taken, and which map to render). This is the write half.
